name: Hai khung cửa
notes: chapters = seconds in film.mp4 where the film waits for a tap, taken from scene.html by stops.py: the title frame (her curtains still closed), one stop in each of the five moments of the day (PAUSE.inBeat into its beat: her note and his side by side), the shared note on the joined window (PAUSE.extra), the climax (PAUSE.climax: the one clock to tap), and the last frame (the morning behind the letter's veil). Each sits a quarter of a frame into its frame, so a seek shows that frame and round(t * fps) finds its boxes. hints = the scene's own words at those stops (WORDS.cue, ui.next, WORDS.hint, ui.skip); a card can override them with "chapters". reveal = null: no 3D envelope; after the last stop a tap opens the letter. slots.json: hers0-k ... hers4-k and mine0-k ... mine4-k are the hour and city on each note (label, coral for hers, indigo for his), hers0-l ... mine4-l the line under it (caption), note the shared note on the joined window (caption); all fade with the scene (alpha is the 5th number of each box). Compromises: the film is drawn for the demo's day, so its clock hands, skies, lamps and skylines follow Toronto and Hà Nội 11 hours apart (her 7:00, 9:40, 12:20, 15:30, 18:30, both clocks ringing at 7:00); a card names its own hours and cities on the notes, but the clocks in the film keep the demo's times. The notes hang straight (the scene tilts them a degree or so) because the player paints words without rotation. Frames where the clock hands spin fast, and the ringing, are blended from several moments (motion blur) so they do not strobe at 24 frames a second. fonts = the faces the player paints these slots in (latin, latin-ext and vietnamese).
